---
title: "Organic matter in water exercises"
---

Use the [notes](notes.qmd). All numerical inputs below are constructed
teaching examples; use the stated assumptions rather than looking up extra
constants. Predict the direction of change before calculating.

## 1. Two equal metal totals

Waters A and B each contain 2.00 µmol/L dissolved total metal. Free metal is 0.500 µmol/L in A and 0.100 µmol/L in B. Assume only free and organically complexed forms. Find bound fractions.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Subtract free from total, then divide by total.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
A is **75.0% bound**; B is **95.0% bound**. The free-ion amounts differ by a factor of five despite identical totals. This simplified partition does not by itself give a toxicity endpoint.
:::

## 2. Oxygen inventory

In a sealed litre of water, oxygen starts at 9.00 mg/L. Completely oxidise 2.00 mg C/L of CH₂O-like substrate, with no other oxygen terms. Calculate residual O₂.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Demand is carbon mass × 32/12.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
Demand = **5.33 mg O₂/L**; residual = **3.67 mg/L**. The calculation assumes the complete aerobic oxidation can occur and ignores gas exchange and competing processes.
:::

## 3. Incomplete degradation

Only 25% of a 4.00 mg C/L CH₂O-like pool is oxidised during an observation period. Calculate model oxygen consumption. Can you report it as the ultimate demand?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Apply the accessible fraction before the stoichiometric ratio.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
Oxidised carbon = 1.00 mg C/L, so consumption is **2.67 mg O₂/L**. Complete oxidation of the entire pool would require 10.67 mg O₂/L. The period-specific consumption is not the ultimate demand.
:::

## 4. Interpret a dark-water change

Water becomes darker while DOC changes little. What chemical explanations and measurements would you consider?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Carbon quantity and optical properties are different observables.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Worked solution"}
Changes in molecular composition, chromophoric groups, particle content, or iron-associated colour could alter absorption per unit carbon. Compare spectra/absorbance, DOC, filtration, iron, and pH. Do not infer a unique source, degradation rate, or toxicity from colour alone.
:::
